title: docker exec
definition: The CLI command that runs a new, secondary command inside an already running container. It is the primary tool used for entering a live container to debug it.
simpleExplanation: Opening a magical trapdoor into a running box. You can step inside the container, walk around, look at the files, and run commands, all while the main app continues to run undisturbed.
realWorldExample: A database container is running. You want to check the tables. You type `docker exec -it my-db bash`. You are instantly transported into the container's terminal, where you can run SQL commands directly.

basic: Can you use `docker exec` to enter a container that is currently Stopped?
intermediate: What do the `-i` and `-t` flags do in `docker exec -it`?

answers.question: Enter stopped container?
answers.answer: No. The container must be actively running for `exec` to work.

answers.question: What are -i and -t?
answers.answer: `-i` (Interactive) keeps the input stream open so you can type. `-t` (TTY) allocates a pseudo-terminal so the output looks like a normal, formatted command prompt.

tableData.title: Crucial Command Flags
rows: Interactive. Keep STDIN open even if not attached.
Allocate a pseudo-TTY (gives you a terminal prompt).
Username or UID to run the command as (e.g., to run as root).
Working directory inside the container for the command.
